sources.citation: SIL Language & Culture Archives OAI-PMH harvest (April 2024): all 39 records tagged Sos Kundi [sdk].
sources.note: Bibliographic only. The SIL archive holds for [sdk]: the dictionary (oai:sil.org:199876 = archive entry 85276), the survey report (2009 ms and 2013 ESR), and 37 vernacular readers/health booklets (Janzen, Sipili et al., 2008-2015). No organised phonology data, phonology essentials, grammar sketch or orthography paper is listed for Sos Kundi.

sources.citation: Janzen, Correna & Elvira Corbalan (compilers). 2019 [published online 2018-03-29 as 'rough draft'; PDF dated 2019-02-06]. Sos Kundi - English - Tok Pisin Dictionary. SIL International (Webonary). 457 pp., 3371 entries.
sources.note: Nothing. Front matter is title, CC licence, compilers, acknowledgements; then entries A-Y with English/Tok Pisin glosses and example sentences. a full-text search for stress/accent|accent|tone|tonal|syllable|phonolog|pronunciation|orthograph over the full text: zero relevant hits. Headwords carry no stress marks. downloaded from the the Internet Archive (webonary.org is an automated-access block-could not be reached by automated download).

sources.note: Nothing; catalogue metadata read from Internet Archive copy (2024-07-31 and 2020-07-20), used to locate the PDFs.

sources.citation: Webonary 'Sos Kundi Dictionary' site, pages Language > Phonology, Language > Grammar, Overview > Alphabet, Overview > Introduction, Overview > Entries explained (SIL International, 2018-2019).
sources.note: The 'Phonology' and 'Grammar' pages are empty placeholders (heading only, no content). Alphabet page: 'There are 22 letters: a aa b d e g i ii j k l m n o p r s t u v w y'. Introduction: ~3,500 speakers, East Sepik, compiled over ten years by Janzen & Corbalan. No mention of stress anywhere.

sources.citation: Richardson, Dan & Ian Tupper. 2013. The cases of Sos Kundi and Ambakich: Drawing language boundaries and assigning names. SIL Electronic Survey Reports 2013-005. Dallas: SIL International. 21 pp.
sources.note: Nothing on phonology. Sociolinguistic survey (May 2007): language names, boundaries, reported/observed intelligibility, WORDSURV lexical similarity (Sos Kundi villages 88-98%, Sos Kundi/Keak ~68%). The word 'accent' occurs once in the lay sense ('it's a different accent/they sound slightly different'). Identifies Sos Kundi with Staalsen's 'Kwaruwi Kwundi' and Laycock's East Sawos dialect. downloaded from the the Internet Archive (sil.org could not be reached by automated download).

sources.citation: ISO 639-3 Registration Authority. 2008. Change Request 2008-022: split [sic] Malinguat into Keak [keh] and Sos Kundi [sdk] (adopted 2009-01-16). Submitted by Dan Richardson (SIL PNG). 8 pp.
sources.note: Nothing; administrative document (not inherently intelligible, 68% lexical similarity, no common literature). No hits for stress/accent/tone/phonolog.

sources.citation: Laycock, Donald C. 1965. The Ndu language family (Sepik District, New Guinea). Pacific Linguistics C-1. Canberra: ANU. Ch. 14 'Notes on the Sawos language', pp. 143-144; sec. 5.2 'Stress', pp. 29-30.
sources.note: Nothing for Sawos/Sos Kundi: 14.13 'it was not possible to elicit material in Sawos. Only two speakers of the language were encountered, and these only briefly'. The stress section (5.2, pp. 29-30, primary/secondary stress ranking) describes Wosera Abelam only.

sources.citation: Glottolog 5.1/5.3 languoid page sosk1235 (Hammarstrom et al.).
sources.note: Nothing. Lists only classification references (Aikhenvald 2015, Laycock 1965, Staalsen 1975, Richardson & Tupper 2013, Jendraschek 2012: 4-8); no grammar, sketch or phonology for [sdk]; alternative names Agbane, Kwaruwi Kwundi, Sawos, Sepik Plains, Soskundi, Tshuosh, Tshwosh.
